jei.nookworks.info.stone_maker: Makes a cobblestone a second from power (20 FE/t). Put a container below it to collect.
jei.nookworks.info.generator: Burns any furnace fuel for 40 FE/t and shares the power evenly with connected machines and cables. With its slot empty it burns liquid fuel piped into its tank: vegetable oil or biodiesel, as long as each other.
jei.nookworks.info.diesel_generator: Burns biodiesel alone, at 240 FE/t - six Generators' worth - and gets twice a Generator's power out of it: 1,280 FE a mB, so a bucket runs it about four and a half minutes. The biodiesel goes into its tank of four buckets by Copper Pipe, by a bucket or bottle clicked on it, or put in its slot; the empties come back to the hand, or out of the slot into a container below. It shares its power evenly with the machines and cables joined to it, as a Generator does. A comparator reads how full its tank is.
jei.nookworks.info.energy_cable: Carries power from Generators - and other mods' generators - to the machines it joins, shared evenly among them; when there is not enough for all, each gets its turn. A network is followed through up to 512 cables by default (the Energy Cable Reach setting); a Generator on one that runs on further says so on its screen. Sneak-right-click a side with the Wrench to disconnect it.
jei.nookworks.info.mob_bottle: Right-click a mob at half health or less to catch it (not bosses, the warden, the elder guardian, vexes or players; a pet only by its owner). The whole mob goes in: released onto a block, the same mob comes back out, with its name, age, trades and whatever it carries. A villager leaves its bed and workstation behind; one never traded with also loses its job and trades once let out - trade with it once first to keep them. Or brew it with an egg in the Spawn Egg Brewer for a spawn egg; the mob is used up and the empty bottle comes back.
jei.nookworks.info.barter_terminal: Lets piglins live outside the Nether. Build a closed room, its floor 1x1 to 4x4 and 2 to 4 high inside, floored with the Nether's ground (nylium, netherrack, soul soil...), its walls and roof of anything, glass included - but a door in them must be iron: piglins open wooden and copper ones. Set a Ventilation Fan in its wall, its guard inwards, and put the terminal against the fan's back, or join them with Ducts (16 at most). Powered, it makes the Nether's air and blows it into the room: the piglins in it do not turn into zombified piglins, as in the Nether. A Mob Bottle with a piglin in it, put in its bottle slot, lets the piglin out into the room (an empty bottle takes one back out); a room takes three piglins a floor block. Gold put in is handed to the piglins with a hand free, and what they throw back is drawn in and passed into the container below. Should the power fail or the room be broken open, the air lasts five minutes; a gap shows where the air leaks out.
jei.nookworks.info.trading_counter: A shop counter a villager trades over by itself. Stand a grown villager with trades in the cell behind it - bring it in a minecart or boat, or click the counter with a Mob Bottle holding one (an empty one takes it back, at half health or less, as a bottle does anywhere) - and keep it there, as in a trading hall's 1x1 cell: the counter is as high as a fence to climb, so the villager does not hop over it. Tick the trades to make in its screen. Once a second it makes the first ticked trade that is in stock, paid for, and has room for its goods: payment goes in from the top or the sides (by hopper or by hand), and the goods come out of its bottom. The prices are those the villager gives whoever set the counter down, their discounts included, and the trades give the villager its experience and levels, and that player reputation, as trades by hand do. Stock comes back as vanilla's does: the villager restocks at its own workstation in working hours, twice a day at most, so set one within its reach. It waits while the villager sleeps or a player trades with it, and under a redstone signal. The round arrow over the list re-rolls the trades of a villager never traded with, as breaking its workstation and setting it back would (a librarian's book rolls again). A comparator reads how full its slots are, as a chest's. Tick "Stop when prices rise" at the top right and a trade whose price demand has raised waits until it is back at its own price.
jei.nookworks.info.spawner_control: Place a Spawner Link Sender next to spawners, right-click it with a Spawner Link Receiver to pair, set a Spawner Controller on top of the receiver (not beside or under it) and power the receiver with FE. The controller's screen lights while it runs. Its GUI sets on/off, interval, count, nearby cap, spawn rules (the mob's own, or none: then it spawns wherever there is room - light, ground and all ignored) and whether a player is needed. Power follows what it is asked for: 20 FE/t a spawner at the defaults (four every ten seconds), as much more as it spawns more often or more at a time, twice that for ignoring the rules and twice again for needing nobody near; the screen shows what it uses. Without enough power the spawners go back to spawning as vanilla's do. Switched off (in the screen or by redstone), its spawners stay off, at no cost and even without power.
jei.nookworks.info.spawner_pickup: Mine a spawner with a Silk Touch hammer to pick it up with its mob (a pickaxe gets nothing).
jei.nookworks.info.elevator: Stack elevators in the same column with 2 blocks of space above each: jump to go up, sneak to go down.
jei.nookworks.info.item_warp: Items dropped on or hoppered into a sender go to the nearest receiver in the same column, up to 64 blocks above or below (a setting). Only receivers set down by whoever set the sender down take from it: anyone else's in the column is passed over. The receiver puts them into the container under it; with none there it drops them below it (on top, if a block is under it).

jei.nookworks.info.laser: Uses 400 FE/t to hold the beam - ten generators' worth - and 4,000 FE more each time it takes a tree down, which it will not do on an empty buffer. With nothing in the beam's way to cut, burn or hurt it stands by on 2 FE/t, the beam off, and fires the moment something comes into it. Fires up to 8 blocks ahead (a redstone signal stops it). Fells a whole natural tree when it hits the trunk - the Nether's huge fungi too - hurts anything in the beam, and may set other flammable blocks on fire unless they have Fireproof Coating. With its redstone control set to "Run with a signal" and a Nested Timer pulsing it, it draws nothing at all between pulses.
jei.nookworks.info.planter: Plants the seeds and saplings it holds into the 3x5 area in front of it, at its own height (the soil is one block lower). 20 FE per plant; hoppers can refill it.
jei.nookworks.info.nourished_soil: Dirt fed with bone meal. Till it with a hoe and water it like any other bed, and what grows on it starts out growing about four times as fast - but it is spent by degrees over roughly three hours, slowing as it goes - paler and drier, the white flecks of bone meal gone - and ends as plain farmland. Jumping onto it or falling on it ruins it outright, as it would farmland; walking across it does not.

jei.nookworks.info.mercury: Toxic: touching it poisons you and makes you dizzy. Only Nookworks' iron Mercury Tanks and Pipes hold it; a bucket of it goes into a Mercury Tank, not into a machine. A Mercury Tank holds 16 buckets and keeps them when broken: a Mercury Bucket pours one in, an empty bucket takes one out, and an empty hand or a comparator reads it. Machines draw mercury from, and send it to, Mercury Tanks beside them or joined by Mercury Pipe. A network is followed through 512 pipes at most; tanks and machines further on are not reached.
jei.nookworks.info.cinnabar: Cinnabar is the rock of the sulfur caves, deep underground, and nowhere else: the start of everything mercury. Roasted in a Sealed Retort it gives up its mercury, and sulfur dust besides. Sulfur, from the same caves, crushes to sulfur dust too. A Nook Dowsing Rod points the way to the caves.
jei.nookworks.info.distiller: Build a tower: Vacuum Distiller at the bottom, 2 Distillation Columns, a Condenser on top. Most of the mercury comes back and leaves through Mercury Pipes.
jei.nookworks.info.caustic_soda: Boil a bucket of sea water dry in the Sealed Retort for Crude Salt, sift it into Salt, then run the Salt through the Electrolytic Cell: as a mercury cell it makes Caustic Soda of salt and water, losing only a little of its mercury.
jei.nookworks.info.fine_paper: Crush logs into Wood Chips in the Crusher, cook them in the Sealed Retort with Caustic Soda and Sulfur Dust (in its reagent slots) into pulp, and press four pulp into one sheet.
jei.nookworks.info.printing_press: Load Fine Paper and the four process inks - cyan, magenta, yellow and black dye - into their own slots, pick a design, then press Print. It does not start on its own. A design you cannot afford is dimmed. Hoppers feed the matching slots and take copies from the bottom. Labels are printed on the Labels page: put a sample in the slot under the Print button (one sheet and a drop of each ink make 8 labels showing it), or type up to 8 letters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9) for 8 labels saying them, which take a sheet and a drop of black ink alone. Photos are printed on the Photos page, from a Camera you carry: see the Camera's page.
jei.nookworks.info.label: Printed on the Printing Press, with the picture of a sample or up to 8 letters. Use it on the side of a chest, a barrel or any block to stick it there, where you press it. Right-clicking it uses the block behind; hit it to take it off. Sneak as you stick it to put it in the very middle of the face.
jei.nookworks.info.velarium_nugget: Velarium never forms an ore body: the only trace of it is what an amalgam leaves behind in the Vacuum Distiller, and it comes out a nugget at a time. Nine nuggets make an ingot.
message.nookworks.world_config_moved: Nookworks: this world's own settings were moved to its syncedconfig folder, where Minecraft 26.3 reads them. They take effect the next time the world is opened.
tooltip.nookworks.red_hot.hot: Still hot: %s s left to quench it
jei.nookworks.info.red_hot_velarium_ingo: A Velarium Ingot heated in a furnace, blast furnace or Electric Furnace comes out red-hot, one at a time. Too hot to hold: taken by hand it burns and is dropped, and it cannot be picked up while it glows. Within half a minute, feed it into a cauldron of vegetable oil - by a hopper, a dropper or a dispenser, or let it fall in - and it is quenched into a Tempered Velarium Ingot, a level of the oil spent (a bucket does three). What comes out goes into a container under the cauldron, or onto its rim. Too late, and it has cooled into a plain ingot: heat it again. Build the line before you light the furnace.
jei.nookworks.info.tempered_velarium_ing: A Velarium Ingot quenched in oil (see the Red-Hot Velarium Ingot). Velarium tools and armour are made of it and mended with it; barrels, gears and blocks still take plain ingots.
jei.nookworks.info.reinforced_rod: A breeze rod sheathed in two Brass Ingots: the handle Velarium tools are made on - a wooden stick is no match for their heads. Breeze rods come from the Breezes of trial chambers.
jei.nookworks.info.brass: Heat two Copper Ingots and one Zinc Ingot in the Sealed Retort to get three Brass Ingots (copper in the charge slot, copper and zinc in the reagent slots). Zinc comes from Raw Zinc, which the Sifter now and then finds in gravel and in Deepslate Gravel (cobbled deepslate put through the Crusher). Mercury eats brass, so it has no place in mercury tanks or pipes.
jei.nookworks.info.machine_chassis: The blackened steel frame the powered machines are built on: the Generator, Crusher, Compressor, Stone Maker, Laser, Electric Furnace, Motor, Printing Press, Sealed Retort, Electrolytic Cell and Barter Terminal all start from one. A Scrap Bale can stand in for its iron block.
jei.nookworks.info.compressor: Packs nine of a thing into one, as the crafting grid's 3x3 recipe for it would: nine nuggets into an ingot, nine ingots into a block, nine Scrap into a Scrap Bale. It waits until it has nine; what it makes leaves from its bottom. Feed it by hopper, by another mod's item pipe, or by hand in its screen. It runs on 20 FE/t, two seconds a press. It has four input slots, one kind of thing each, so a few of one thing waiting for their ninth do not stop the rest.
jei.nookworks.info.recycler: Shreds worn-out metal things and gives back half the metal they were made of: iron and copper come back as Scrap, gold as Gold Nuggets. The more worn a tool or armour piece, the less comes back. Metal junk only: ingots, metal blocks and copper building blocks stay out, as do stone, dirt, wood and Netherite. Two blocks tall: load it at the top; what it makes goes into a container under it, or with none there drops out below, on top or beside it. What it takes is tagged #nookworks:recyclable, for a Precision Sorter. It runs on 40 FE/t; a piece takes one to six seconds, by how much metal is in it. Nookworks' own metal things go in too - gears, hooks, bookends, pipes, machines.
jei.nookworks.info.baler: A press for packing scrap tight. It does nothing on its own: it is the part a Recycler is built from, with a Crusher and a Compressor.
jei.nookworks.info.scrap: What the Recycler gives back. Smelt it for an Iron Nugget, pack nine into a Scrap Bale (a bale stands in for the iron block in a Machine Chassis), or build with it: Corrugated Sheets and Patched Sheet Metal.
jei.nookworks.info.rusting_scrap: Bare scrap rusts where it stands, as copper weathers: dull, then patched with rust, then rust all over. Wax it with Honeycomb to keep it as it is; scrape it with an axe to take a stage back (or the wax off).
jei.nookworks.info.corrugated_sheet: A thin sheet, set against the face you click; laid flat, its ridges run the way you face. Eight sheets and a dye make eight painted ones, which do not rust. Sneak and right-click one with a Wrench to move it to the middle of its block, where a glass pane stands, and back.

jei.nookworks.info.liquid_experience: 20 mB is one experience point, the same rate other mods use. It is tagged #c:experience, so their pipes, tanks and machines take it and ours take theirs. Standing in it burns, and a mob killed by it counts as killed by the nearest player, so player-only drops still fall - but not a villager, a trader, a pet or a named mob, which no one is blamed for.
jei.nookworks.info.experience_tank: Holds 16 buckets (800 points). The tap on its front faces you when you place it: turn it with an empty hand and the tank pours out as a stream of experience orbs until it runs dry or you turn it back. A bucket or a bottle fills or empties it, and a comparator reads how full it is. It pushes nothing out itself: an Experience Pipe set to pull with the Wrench draws it into a line - to a Repair Box, say. Broken, it lets what it holds out as orbs: it does not keep it as a Copper Tank does.
jei.nookworks.info.experience_pipe: Carries Liquid Experience, ours or another mod's, from what pushes it out - an Absorption Pad, the Sealed Retort, the Electric Furnace - to a tank, a Repair Box or another mod's machine; its glass glows green while experience runs through. An Experience Tank pushes nothing out: to send what it holds down a line, sneak-right-click the pipe's side against it with the Wrench until it says pulling (a steel flange shows on that arm). The pipe then draws from the tank, 400 mB a tick, while something down the line takes it, and pours nothing back. Used on a pipe without sneaking, the Wrench lets what it holds out as orbs.
jei.nookworks.info.absorption_pad: Pulls in experience orbs from 6 blocks away, and takes the experience of whoever stands on it. A redstone signal - a lever beside it - switches it off, and its intake goes dark. It pushes what it collects into any pipe or tank beside it, and a pipe that pulls can draw from it too; nothing can be poured back in. It keeps only 100 points itself, so set a pipe or tank beside it.
jei.nookworks.info.warp_anchor: While on, nothing warps into or out of the space around it: 4 blocks to each side and 2 up and down, a spawner's spawning area with a block more above and below. Endermen and shulkers cannot teleport there, so endermen stay out of a spawner room and a shulker spawner can be made into a farm; ender pearls, Lode Pearls and chorus fruit do not take you in or out. Elevators, the Dock-a-Daemon Door and Item Warps work as usual. Right-click to turn it on and off.

item.nookworks.lode_pearl.anchored: A Warp Anchor stops warping here
gui.nookworks.repair_box.hint: Put in worn gear to mend it
jei.nookworks.info.repair_box: A chest that repairs worn gear with FE and Liquid Experience, Mending or not. It draws experience from a tank or pipe beside it; a tank further off feeds it through an Experience Pipe set to pull from the tank (sneak-right-click that side of the pipe with the Wrench). A bucket or bottle of Liquid Experience clicked on it pours in, and the empty comes back. Two side by side, facing the same way, join into one large box (sneak to place one that stays single): twelve slots, and the power and experience of both halves go to whatever needs them. Only finished items come out, so a hopper can cycle gear through it.
jei.nookworks.info.wrench: Right-click a block to turn it, sneak to turn it back. On a pipe or cable, sneak-right-click the side you point at to disconnect it (the arm, or the face of the middle for a side with no arm); do it again to connect it. A pipe of the same kind on that side is disconnected with it. On a Copper or Experience Pipe, a side against a tank or machine goes round three ways: connected, pulling, disconnected. Pulling, the pipe draws what that block holds into the line - from one tank into another, say - and never pours anything into it; a steel flange on the arm shows it. Used on a pipe that holds something, it flushes it: water and oil are poured away, experience comes out as orbs - to switch a line to another fluid. On a Corrugated Sheet, sneak-right-click moves it to the middle of its block, where a glass pane stands, and back.
jei.nookworks.info.fireproof_coating: Right-click a flammable block - planks, logs, wool, a bookshelf - to coat it: it never catches fire again, from flames or from lava. A pot coats 64 blocks. The coating goes with the block when a piston moves it, and comes off when the block is broken or scrubbed with Soap. While you hold the pot, coated blocks nearby sparkle.
jei.nookworks.info.crate: A 9-slot box that keeps what is in it when broken, as a shulker box does: an early way to move house. Crates and shulker boxes do not go inside one.
jei.nookworks.info.magnet: Right-click to switch it on. While on, from anywhere in your inventory, it pulls dropped items and experience within 8 blocks to you (the Advanced Magnet: 16) - what you can see, not through a wall. Sneak to pause it, to drop things. Items another player is to have stay where they are.
jei.nookworks.info.hammer: Mines the 3x3 square facing you, at 40% of the matching pickaxe's speed, with four times its durability. Sneak to mine one block (the settings say when 3x3 mining happens). Round the block you hit it takes only what it mines properly and nothing much harder - no chests or furnaces, no Budding Amethyst. Earthmover adds dirt, sand, gravel and wood. With Silk Touch it picks up a spawner.
jei.nookworks.info.building_wand: Right-click a block face to spread that block across the flat surface, up to 32 at a time, out of your inventory.
jei.nookworks.info.trash_can: Takes nothing from your hand: only a hopper or a pipe can feed it, and only while it is getting a redstone signal. With no signal it refuses items outright, so the line backs up instead of quietly emptying. What does go in is gone for good.

jei.nookworks.info.precision_sorter: 18 filter slots, and two switches. Exclude: ON sends registered items out of the other side instead. Exact: ON tells a damaged, enchanted or renamed item apart from a fresh one; OFF, the default, treats them as the same. Tags…: put a sample item in, tick what to sort by, and Register. Each tag becomes an entry of its own, marked #, that catches everything in the tag (an iron ingot's c:ingots/iron, or every plank at once with minecraft:planks); the line above the tags, the sample's mod, becomes an entry marked @ that catches every item of that mod (all of Minecraft's own for a vanilla sample). Like the Item Sorter it draws from a container on top of it, and keeps a hopper's pace until a Sorter Gear is fitted in its gear slot. Items registered in the red Keep Out row are never drawn in and stay in the container above; so does anything the inventory it would go to can never hold (a bundle bound for a Storage Barrel), rather than stopping the sorter. A whole tag or mod can be kept out too: tick it under Tags… and press Keep these out. Click the row's sign to turn it round: then only what is in it is drawn in, and the rest stays above.
jei.nookworks.info.item_sorter: Items fed in from any side, or drawn from a chest or other container on top of it as a hopper draws them, leave by the right-hand outlet if they are registered in its nine filter slots, and by the left otherwise - into the inventory on that side, or out onto the ground. If that inventory is full it waits, and draws nothing more from above until there is room. On its own it keeps a hopper's pace, one item every 0.4 seconds; fit a Sorter Gear in its gear slot to sort faster. For tags, whole mods, an exclude list or exact matching, make it a Precision Sorter. Items registered in the red Keep Out row are never drawn in and stay in the container above; so does anything the inventory it would go to can never hold (a bundle bound for a Storage Barrel), rather than stopping the sorter. Click the row's sign to turn it round: then only what is in it is drawn in, and the rest stays above.
jei.nookworks.info.sorter_gear: Fitted into the gear slot of an Item Sorter or a Precision Sorter, it sorts faster: gold an item every 0.2 seconds, diamond every 0.1, netherite four a tick, Velarium a whole stack a tick. Each is made from the one before, and it comes out again as it went in. The front of the sorter shows the gear fitted.

jei.nookworks.info.storage_barrel: Storage Barrels open with a block on top and point wherever you place them, including up and down. Iron holds a double chest's worth, and each tier up holds far more. Break one and its contents spill like a chest's; one holding more than %s stacks cannot be broken by a player - with any tool, or in creative - until you take some out. Shulker boxes and bundles do not go in, nor anything else a shulker box refuses (another mod's backpack); a Crate does, full or not.

jei.nookworks.info.rare_seed: The seed of Dawnwood, a conifer thought long extinct. It grows nowhere in the world; now and then one turns up when dirt is sifted, and the Wandering Trader sometimes has one. Plant it like a sapling and it grows into a tall, narrow tree whose leaves drop more seeds.
jei.nookworks.info.support: A squared timber in four shapes: a post, a beam along the top of the block, a wall bracket with a brace, or a post standing against the wall. Placed against a wall it is a bracket; on a floor or ceiling, a post. Use an axe on it to change the shape. Thin Rope ties round a bracket's brace, as round a fence post.
jei.nookworks.info.rope: A rope to climb, like a ladder. Hang it under a block - a fence, a top slab or a support's beam will do - and use more rope on it to lengthen it from the bottom; use it with an empty hand to take the bottom length back. Take away what it hangs from and the whole rope comes down. It hangs in water too.
jei.nookworks.info.chair: Right-click a chair to sit on it; sneak to get up. Under a low ceiling you sit a little lower, and with no room above the seat at all you cannot sit.
jei.nookworks.info.stool: A low stool with no back. Right-click it to sit down, a little lower than on a chair; sneak to get up again. Under a low ceiling you sit lower still, and with no room at all above the seat you cannot sit.
jei.nookworks.info.bench: A long seat with no back, as low as a stool. Benches set side by side, of any wood, join into one long bench on legs at its two ends; each block of it seats one. Right-click it to sit down; sneak to get up again. Set down beside another, a bench faces as that one does (sneak to set it facing you). Sneak-use a Wrench on the end between two benches to keep them apart, or to join them again.
jei.nookworks.info.wall_shelf: A board the size of a trapdoor on two black iron brackets, hung on a wall: use it on a wall's face, or set it down looking at one. Its top is flat, so a lantern, a candle, a flower pot or anything else stands on it. Shelves side by side facing the same way join into one long shelf, with brackets at its ends only. It comes down when the wall behind it goes. Made of a trapdoor and two iron nuggets. Sneak-use a Wrench on the end between two shelves to keep them apart, or to join them again.
jei.nookworks.info.desk: A top on four legs, in every wood. Desks set side by side, of any wood, join into one long desk (an L or a square too), its legs at the corners only; it can be waterlogged. Sneak-use a Wrench on the edge between two desks to keep them apart, or to join them again.
jei.nookworks.info.tuned: This server changes the machines: power use x%1$s, work time x%2$s, Generator output x%3$s. The figures above are the defaults; a machine's screen shows what it works by.
jei.nookworks.info.dice: Right-click it, or give it a redstone pulse, and it is tossed up and tumbles as a real die does, coming to rest on 1-6 in a second or so, where it lands and turned as it landed; a comparator reads 0 while it rolls, then the number. Rolled in the air from the hand, it shows everyone nearby the number over their hotbar. A dispenser throws it: it lands in front and rolls as a placed die - knock it loose with a piston and bring it back round with a Magnet Chest and a hopper.
jei.nookworks.info.standing_mirror: A tall mirror in a Dawnwood frame that shows what stands before it, as a mirror does: the room, you, and whoever is about. Set it down and its glass faces you; it stands two blocks high. The two nearest mirrors in view within 32 blocks show their reflections, of what is within about 24 blocks of the glass; any others show plain silver. It opens onto nothing; the If Mirror, made with Dice, is the way into the If.
jei.nookworks.info.bookend: A thin L of iron to stand books in. Set it on a block's top: its upright goes on the side of the block you click, and its books' spines face you. A book used on it stands upright against it, spine out, and the next beside it, five to a block; with that full, the row goes on into the block beyond, and on, while there is floor. A book used on any part of the row goes to its end, and an empty hand takes the end's last one back. Take the bookend away and the row falls. Sneak and use a book on a wall's side, and it leans against the wall instead.
jei.nookworks.info.placed_book: Sneak and use a book on the top of a block to lay it down there - a book, an enchanted book, a written book or a book and quill - up to three in a pile; on a wall's side, it stands leant against the wall. Each keeps itself as it was. Use a pile with an empty hand to take the top one back; broken, or its floor gone, it drops them. To stand books upright in a row, use a Bookend.
jei.nookworks.info.brass_mesh: Fit it into the Sifter's brass-framed slot. Sifting takes twice as long, but fewer rolls come up empty: the small things an ordinary mesh lets fall - nuggets, raw zinc, gems and seeds - turn up more often, and flint, clay and the rest as often as ever. It works on what the Sifter sifts by itself, not on sifting by hand, and only on what has small things in it: Crude Salt sifts as before, at the usual pace. Take it out to sift the ordinary way again.
jei.nookworks.info.sifter: Right-click it holding gravel, sand, dirt or the like to sift one by hand: what it gives pops out on top. Fed by a hopper, or through its screen (right-click with an empty hand), it sifts by itself, with no power, and puts what it gives into a chest or hopper under it; with none there, it drops out. A Brass Mesh in its brass-framed slot finds more of the small things, at half the speed, and only when it sifts by itself. Look up the Sifter's uses (U) for everything it sifts and what each gives.
jei.nookworks.info.lode_pearl: Use an ender pearl on a lodestone and it becomes a Lode Pearl bound to it (one a click; pearls bound to the same lodestone stack). A Lode Pearl used on another lodestone is bound to that one instead. Throw it and, wherever it lands - even down into the void - you are taken to that lodestone, in any dimension - the If too - and set down gently: no damage. One use. If the lodestone is gone, nobody moves and a plain ender pearl comes back to your hands; turned away (by a claim, or with no room there), the Lode Pearl itself comes back, still bound. Soap in the crafting grid washes the binding off. Lodestones have names: set down, one is named after where it stands (or by its anvil name), and an empty-handed right-click on it renames it. A pearl is called after its lodestone.
jei.nookworks.info.dark_matter: Puts out the light round it: from the layer under it to three above, as far as water would spread from it (seven blocks along the ground), everything is at light 0 - outdoors at noon too, and whatever lamps shine in from outside. Monsters spawn there by day, zombies do not burn, and crops neither grow nor can be planted. Put anything that gives light inside that area (a torch, a lit lamp) and the dark lifts, all of it, until the light goes again.
jei.nookworks.info.daemon_door: One door to every dimension you have been to. Set it into a wall - the ten blocks round its doorway full blocks - put a Destination Panel on the wall beside it, and pick where it opens onto: the Nether, the End, the If, other mods' dimensions. Open it and walk in from the front - the side you set it down from, where the sliding leaf hangs; from behind, or with the panel set to Off, it is an ordinary door. Each player picks their own. Open, it shows the gate of the world beyond: the Nether's swirl, the End's stars, the If's mirror, another mod's own portal. The first trip to a dimension sets a return door there in a frame of stone bricks, near where you last were in it; it leads back home, and can be picked up and set into a wall elsewhere in its dimension. One door stands in each dimension at a time.
jei.nookworks.info.if_mirror: The way into the If: the overworld again, from another seed, with nothing of other mods in it. Set it down and throw Dice at it six times; the six faces are the If's number, and the same number is the same world in any save. Then right-click its glass with an empty hand to go through. The first trip sets the If's own mirror down, its way home; in the If, a compass points to it. One mirror stands at home and one in the If. Only the mirror, the Dock-a-Daemon Door and a Lode Pearl go in or out: no portal opens there.
jei.nookworks.info.electric_furnace: Smelts whatever a furnace smelts, in half the time, on 40 FE/t: a coal's worth of Generator power smelts sixteen items, twice what the coal would in a furnace - and a Generator on piped oil or biodiesel keeps it going by itself. Input from any side; the results go into the container below. The experience is kept as Liquid Experience, up to a bucket (50 points): an Experience Pipe draws it off, and a glass bottle or bucket put in the slot with a faint bottle drawn in it is filled with it; what no longer fits comes out on top as experience orbs.
jei.nookworks.info.electric_furnace.with: Smelts whatever a furnace smelts, in half the time, on 40 FE/t: a coal's worth of Generator power smelts sixteen items, twice what the coal would in a furnace - and a Generator on piped oil or biodiesel keeps it going by itself. Input from any side; the results go into the container below. It keeps the experience, up to 50 points; what no longer fits comes out on top as experience orbs, and broken, it lets out what it held as orbs.
jei.nookworks.info.electrolytic_cell: A current through water, on 80 FE/t. As a mercury cell - the way caustic soda was made for a century - it turns Salt and water into Caustic Soda: brine flows over a pool of mercury, the sodium goes into the mercury as amalgam, and water washes it back out as caustic soda. It needs 250 mB of mercury standing in it, drawn from its Mercury Pipes, and loses only 5 mB a run. It also wins zinc from raw zinc (half the time an extra ingot), and takes the tarnish off copper: exposed, weathered and oxidized copper of every shape, waxed or not, statues too, comes back bright. Water by Copper Pipe or bucket; results into the container below.
jei.nookworks.info.liquid_experience_bot: 250 mB of Liquid Experience. Fill it in the slot with a faint glass bottle drawn in it on the Sealed Retort's or the Electric Furnace's screen (a glass bottle in, the filled bottle out; hoppers work too) or by using a glass bottle on an Experience Tank. On an Enchanting Table, one lapis lazuli and no levels turn it into a Bottle o' Enchanting.
jei.nookworks.info.workbench: A crafting table built as a machinist's bench, for a workshop a wooden crafting table looks out of place in: the same 3x3 grid and recipe book, on a table with a drawer, a shelf with a toolbox, and a vise, a blueprint and a hammer on its top. It faces you when you set it down.
jei.nookworks.info.charred_lump: What cooked meat or fish, or a baked potato, becomes if it is cooked again - in a furnace, a smoker, on a campfire or a Grill. Not food any more; with an amethyst block, it makes Dark Matter.
jei.nookworks.info.vine: Use Fine Shears on a vine and it stops spreading, as cave vines do when their tip is cut: the vine cut grows no further. Cut the ends of a curtain of vines and it hangs as it is. Vanilla's shears leave a vine growing.
jei.nookworks.drying.how: Hung on a Thin Rope, under open sky
message.nookworks.wrench.sheet_centered: Sheet moved to the middle of the block
message.nookworks.wrench.sheet_against: Sheet set back against its face
message.nookworks.wrench.furniture_apart: Kept apart from the one beside it
message.nookworks.wrench.furniture_joine: Joined to the one beside it
nookworks.configuration.timber.fastLeafD: When a tree is felled, its leaves fall within seconds instead of decaying slowly.
nookworks.configuration.timber.instantLe: With Fast Leaf Decay on, a felled tree's leaves all fall at once, the moment the tree comes down.
nookworks.configuration.storageBreakStac: A Storage Barrel holding more stacks than this cannot be broken by a player, with any tool or in creative; take some out first.
jei.nookworks.info.retort_experience: Every charge leaves experience behind, as a furnace's does: the Retort keeps it as Liquid Experience (up to 1 bucket) and pushes it into an Experience Pipe or tank beside it; what no longer fits comes out on top as orbs. Other mods' pipes can draw it out too. Broken, it pours what it held out as orbs.
jei.nookworks.info.retort_experience.wit: Every charge leaves experience behind, as a furnace's does: the Retort keeps it, up to 50 points, and what no longer fits comes out on top as orbs. A pipe of another mod can draw it out as liquid experience. Broken, it pours what it held out as orbs.
gui.nookworks.storage.order.hint: Click for the next, right-click for the one before
gui.nookworks.storage.direction.hint: Click to turn the order round
gui.nookworks.recipe_choice: Other recipes match: %s things to choose from
jei.nookworks.info.hanging_planter: Hang it under a block, a chain or a rope (Thin Rope suits it) and its plant trails down over the bowl. The plant grows further down over time, or with bone meal, up to 3 blocks, and stops at anything in its way. It falls if what holds it is taken away.
jei.nookworks.info.thin_rope: A cord to hang things from. Hang it under a block and use more on it to lengthen it; use it with an empty hand to take the bottom length back. It cannot be climbed. Its end takes a Hanging Planter, a Filament Bulb or a lantern, or something hung up by a bit of string: a bottle, a fish or kelp to dry, a bunch of flowers, an ear of corn, a sprig of sweet berries, glow berries as a block of their cave vine (bare at first, as under a ceiling, and alight where it bears berries), a mob's head or the dragon egg, or a banner, by a cord from both ends of its bar. Used on a fence post, iron or copper bars, a lightning rod or an end rod, a Hook or the brace of a wall bracket, it is tied there and paid out as you walk; used on another of them within 16 blocks it is tied off, hanging slack between the two - a Thin Rope for each block. It is not tied through something in its way: a fence's middle post, the rail between two posts side by side, a wall. Hang things along it by using them on the rope; a lantern, lit or put out, hangs whole by its own loop - sneak and use it with an empty hand to put it out where it hangs, flint and steel or a fire charge to light it again. Hung glow berries grow down as their vine does, up to five blocks, until something is in the way; shears on the tip stop them, bone meal gives a bare piece berries, and an empty hand picks them. A redstone signal at a post - a lever beside it or on the block under it, a powered block or dust next to it; for a Hook or a bracket, its wall or ceiling powered too - switches the Filament Bulbs and lanterns on the lines tied there: on as the signal comes, off as it goes, and by hand between. A banner hangs by its bar, the cloth straight down and its face to you, where the rope is not steep and there is room below for the cloth. Hit a knot to cut the ropes tied at it. A rope tied to a lightning rod comes off when lightning strikes it.
jei.nookworks.info.thin_chain: Thin Rope in iron. Used on a fence post, iron or copper bars, a lightning rod or an end rod, a Hook or the brace of a wall bracket, it is tied there and paid out as you walk; used on another of them within 16 blocks it is tied off, hanging slack between the two - a Thin Chain for each block. It is not tied through something in its way. Whatever hangs on Thin Rope hangs on it the same way: bottles, fish to dry, flowers, berries, a mob's head, the dragon egg, a Filament Bulb, a lantern, a banner. Walk into it or shoot an arrow through it and it rattles and swings a little, then settles; nothing on it falls. Hit a knot to cut the chains and ropes tied at it. Unlike Thin Rope, it cannot be let down from a block. Used on a Drive Wheel and then another, it is a drive belt up to 16 blocks long.
jei.nookworks.info.filament_bulb: A clear glass bulb with a glowing coil in it, on a brass cap and a short flex. It hangs from the underside of a block, a chain, or the end of a Thin Rope (used anywhere on the rope, it goes on its end). Used on a rope strung between fence posts it hangs there, and a row of them makes a string of lights. Use it with an empty hand to switch it off and on; one hung along a rope, sneak and use it (an empty hand not sneaking takes it down). Set down or hung again, it is on. Set down, a redstone signal coming switches it on and going switches it off.
jei.nookworks.info.hook: A small iron hook for a wall or a ceiling (not a floor), with nothing to bump into. Thin Rope ties to it as to a fence post: use the rope on one hook, walk to another post or hook within 16 blocks and use it there, and a line runs across the room. Use sweet berries on it to hang a sprig of the bush: it pricks and slows whatever moves through it, as the bush does - a spider climbing the wall past it too. Glow berries hang as strands of the cave vine with their berries alight, a lamp for a wall or a beam. An empty hand takes the berries back.
jei.nookworks.info.dried_fish: Raw fish hung up on a rope out in the sun dries into Dried Fish in a day of sunshine (kelp dries too, into dried kelp, in half the time; a pufferfish keeps its poison, and is not dried). Only sunny time counts: daylight, open sky, no rain. It is a little better eating than cooked cod, and no parasite survives it.

Set it down facing the sender's way: it takes from your senders on that line
tooltip.nookworks.hint.hub_stone: Carries a redstone signal like dust, to all six sides
tooltip.nookworks.hint.dice: Right-click or pulse it to roll; a comparator reads the number
tooltip.nookworks.hint.wrench: Turns blocks (sneak: the other way); sneak on a pipe's side to disconnect it - against a tank, first to pull from it - and use it on a pipe to flush it
tooltip.nookworks.hint.building_wand: Spreads the block you click across its flat face, up to 32 at a time
tooltip.nookworks.hint.liquid_experience: On an Enchanting Table: a Bottle o' Enchanting, for one lapis and no levels
tooltip.nookworks.hint.absorption_pad: Stand on it to pour your experience in; a redstone signal switches it off
tooltip.nookworks.hint.nested_timer: Right-click to set when it acts, how many pulses, and how far apart
tooltip.nookworks.hint.sifter: Sift dirt, gravel or sand by hand (right-click) or feed it by hopper
tooltip.nookworks.hint.hook: Ties Thin Rope to a wall or ceiling; sweet berries hang on it, and glow berries as a lamp
tooltip.nookworks.hint.thin_chain: Strung between posts as Thin Rope is, and carries the same things; it rattles when something goes through it
tooltip.nookworks.hint.unlit_lantern: Light it with flint and steel or a fire charge
tooltip.nookworks.hint.drive_wheel: Belt it to another with Rope or Thin Chain: one Motor turns every machine on the wheels
tooltip.nookworks.hint.oil_cake: A fertilizer: use it on crops as bone meal
tooltip.nookworks.hint.trash_can: Destroys what a hopper or pipe feeds it while it has a redstone signal; nothing from your hand
message.nookworks.copper_tank.will_not_t: It holds something else, or it is full
message.nookworks.stirring_tank.will_not: Water or vegetable oil pours in while there is room; only biodiesel is taken out
message.nookworks.mercury_bucket.into_ta: Mercury goes into a Mercury Tank; machines draw it from there
message.nookworks.diesel_generator.biodi: A Diesel Generator runs on biodiesel alone
message.nookworks.repair_box.experience_: A Repair Box takes Liquid Experience alone
message.nookworks.repair_box.no_room: No room in the box for that (%s / %s mB)
message.nookworks.copper_tank.too_little: Not enough in the tank to fill that
gui.nookworks.machine.status.unloaded: Waiting for the next chunk to load
gui.nookworks.machine.status.standby: Standing by: nothing in the beam
gui.nookworks.machine.status.protected: Not allowed to plant here: the land is protected
gui.nookworks.machine.status.low_water: Not enough water in the tank
gui.nookworks.machine.status.low_oil: Not enough oil in the tank
gui.nookworks.machine.status.low_oil.det: A batch of biodiesel takes %s mB of vegetable oil: pipe it in, or pour in a bucket
gui.nookworks.machine.status.another_mot: Standing by - another Motor turns it
gui.nookworks.machine.status.room_protec: Its owner may not use the land the room is on: a claim keeps it
gui.nookworks.machine.status.no_fan.deta: Put it against the back of a Ventilation Fan set in the room's wall, or join them with up to 16 Ducts
gui.nookworks.machine.status.room_open.d: The Nether's air is seen leaking out of it in crimson motes. Piglins open wooden and copper doors: use an iron one
gui.nookworks.machine.status.room_size.d: A cuboid, its floor 1x1 to 4x4 and 2 to 4 high inside, with nothing standing in it
gui.nookworks.machine.status.nether_floo: Nylium, netherrack, soul sand or soul soil, blackstone, basalt
gui.nookworks.machine.status.crowded.det: A room takes three piglins a floor block; they are kept, but do not barter
gui.nookworks.machine.status.barter_term: A room takes three piglins a floor block; they are kept, but do not barter
gui.nookworks.machine.status.diesel_gene: It runs on biodiesel alone: pipe it in, or pour in a bucket or bottles
gui.nookworks.machine.status.too_many_ca: A network is followed through %s cables at most: machines further on get no power (the Energy Cable Reach setting)
jei.nookworks.info.water_pump: Set it on water: on 10 FE/t it draws a bucket a second from the source block under it, and pushes the water out of its top and sides into Copper Pipes, tanks and machines. A source with two source neighbours (a 2x2 pool, a lake, the sea) never runs out; a lone one is pumped dry.
jei.nookworks.info.copper_pipe: Carries water from a Water Pump, vegetable oil or biodiesel to anything that takes it - such as the Sealed Retort, which boils each bucket's worth of water down to crude salt when its charge slot is empty. A pipe holds one liquid at a time. Fluid runs briskly up to 256 pipes from where it is drawn off; further than that, it only seeps along. Sneak-right-click a side with the Wrench to disconnect it; a side against a tank or machine turns to pulling first (a steel flange on the arm): the pipe draws what that block holds into the line, a bucket a tick while something down the line takes it, and pours nothing back - the way to move a Copper Tank's contents into another tank. To switch a line to another liquid, empty its pipes with the Wrench: right-click each one (not sneaking).
jei.nookworks.info.sight_glass: A length of Copper Pipe line with a window in it: placed against a pipe's end it lines up with the pipe, and it passes fluid on as a pipe does. The glass shows what runs through it and how much - full when the line runs full or is backed up, low when it trickles, empty when it is dry - so a line that has stopped can be traced. A comparator beside it reads the same.
jei.nookworks.info.valve: Set in a Copper Pipe line, it passes fluid while open and nothing either way while shut: the line before it backs up and the line after it runs dry. Use it to turn it; a redstone signal coming on opens it and going off shuts it, as a trapdoor, so a Nested Timer can meter a line. Its handle lies along the pipe when open and across it when shut.
jei.nookworks.info.copper_tank: Holds sixteen buckets of water, vegetable oil or biodiesel, one at a time, and keeps them when it is broken. The sight glasses down its sides show which and how much. Copper Pipes and machines fill it from any side but the bottom - a Water Pump or Stirring Tank right under it fills it from below - and it pours out of its bottom into a pipe, a machine or another tank under it. A Copper Pipe set to pull with the Wrench draws from it on any side. By hand, buckets and bottles fill it and draw from it. A comparator reads how full it is.
jei.nookworks.info.oil_lamp: An unglazed clay dish with a wick of rush pith lying across it. Pour vegetable oil in from a bottle (it holds four), light the wick with flint and steel, a fire charge or a burning arrow, and put it out with an empty hand. It burns a bottle in about five minutes - a full dish lasts about a day - and goes out when it runs dry. Its light is softer than a torch's.
jei.nookworks.info.unlit_lantern: A lantern gone out: it gives no light, and its glass is sooty where the flame was. Sneak and use a lantern, a soul lantern or a copper lantern with an empty hand to put it out, standing or hanging; flint and steel or a fire charge lights it again. A copper one goes on weathering as a lit one does, and takes wax from a honeycomb. Mined, it stays unlit.
jei.nookworks.info.placed_bottle: Sneak and use a bottle on the top of a block to set it down there - an empty one, a potion, honey, vegetable oil, dragon's breath and more - up to four to a block, each showing the colour of what is in it. Use them with an empty hand to take back the last one set down; break them and they all drop.
jei.nookworks.info.flour: Wheat ground in the Hand Quern (or the Crusher). In the Iron Pot's oil it coats what is fried: Karaage and Fried Fish come out twice as many. At the crafting table it goes into Tonkatsu's coat.
jei.nookworks.info.breadcrumbs: Bread crumbled in the Hand Quern or the Crusher, two crumbs' worth to a loaf. With Flour and an egg it coats a porkchop at the crafting table, for Tonkatsu.
jei.nookworks.info.breaded_pork: A raw porkchop coated in Flour, an egg and Breadcrumbs at the crafting table, two to a chop. Into an Iron Pot of oil: each fries into a Tonkatsu.
jei.nookworks.info.pebbles: Small smooth stones to scatter on a path, a yard or a pond's floor, for the look. Up to four lie in one place: use another on them to add it. They need a whole block's top under them, keep the water they are set down in, and come up at a touch, by hand or pickaxe, as many as lay there. A cobblestone makes four, in the crafting grid or on a stonecutter; four make a cobblestone again.
jei.nookworks.info.rice: Brown rice, sifted out of soil (most of all mud). Plant it in water one block deep on dirt, grass, farmland, mud or clay, and keep the block above it clear: it grows and heads up into that block. Break the ripe gold heads for 2-4 brown rice and the plant heads up again. Bone meal speeds it along. Put it through a Rice Polisher for white rice to cook.
jei.nookworks.info.nested_timer: Sends pulses out of its front: right-click to set how long until the next action (half a second to an hour), how many pulses it sends then, and how far apart. Two pulses make a dispenser pour a water bucket and take the water back. The bars on its meter show roughly how long. A signal into its back or sides holds it. It faces away from you when placed, like a repeater.
gui.nookworks.nested_timer.status.overfl: Pulses past the next action are not sent
gui.nookworks.nested_timer.output: The output: lit while a pulse goes out
jei.nookworks.info.grill: An iron grate on four legs. Set it on a campfire and it stands astride the fire; lay on it anything a campfire cooks - meat, fish, potatoes - four at a time; cooked, they stay on the grate until you take them off with an empty hand (sneak to take everything). An Iron Pot put on it over the fire sits down on the grate and cooks while the campfire burns. Anywhere else it stands on its own legs as a little table with the grate on top. A hopper above lays food on it. Standing on a hopper over a lit campfire, it is heated through the hopper, which takes off what is done.

block.nookworks.drive_wheel.full: This wheel has two belts already
block.nookworks.drive_wheel.not_parallel: The wheels do not turn the same way: set their axles alike
block.nookworks.drive_wheel.not_in_line: The wheels are not in one plane: the belt would run askew
block.nookworks.drive_wheel.too_long: Too long: this belt reaches %s blocks
block.nookworks.drive_wheel.in_the_way: Something is in the belt's way
block.nookworks.drive_wheel.not_here: You cannot tie a belt here
block.nookworks.drive_wheel.belt_here: A drive belt runs through here
jei.nookworks.info.drive_wheel: Put one on a Motor's shaft, and one against each hand-worked machine you want turned, on the side it is driven from (the Hand Quern above or below). Then use Rope (up to 8 blocks) or Thin Chain (up to 16) on one wheel and then on another: the belt is tied taut between them, and one Motor turns every machine its belts reach, up to 8, using 20 FE/t for each machine at work. Belted wheels must turn the same way and stand in one plane, with nothing in between; wheels set end to end on one axle turn together. A belt takes two of its rope or chain a block. Sneak-use a wheel with an empty hand to take its belts off.
jei.nookworks.info.oil_press: A screw press. Load it with sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, melon seeds, corn kernels or rice bran and right-click it with an empty hand to turn the handle (sneak to take out the cakes it holds, or just to check it); every few turns a seed gives up its oil, and now and then an Oil Cake comes out of the spout at its front. Pour the oil off with a glass bottle or a bucket, or let it run into a Copper Pipe beside or under it. The cakes go into a hopper or chest under it, or else one in front of it; with neither they drop out of the spout onto the ground just in front, for a hopper set in the floor there or a Magnet Chest to gather - and with a block in the way they wait inside. Hoppers load it from above and the sides. A Motor set beside it turns the handle for you.
jei.nookworks.info.oil_press.without_kit: A screw press. Load it with sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds or melon seeds and right-click it with an empty hand to turn the handle (sneak to take out the cakes it holds, or just to check it); every few turns a seed gives up its oil, and now and then an Oil Cake comes out of the spout at its front. Pour the oil off with a glass bottle or a bucket, or let it run into a Copper Pipe beside or under it. The cakes go into a hopper or chest under it, or else one in front of it; with neither they drop out of the spout onto the ground just in front, for a hopper set in the floor there or a Magnet Chest to gather - and with a block in the way they wait inside. Hoppers load it from above and the sides. A Motor set beside it turns the handle for you.
jei.nookworks.info.sunflower_seeds: Sifted now and then from dirt; and a sunflower crafted into yellow dye leaves its four seeds in the grid, the petals plucked. Sown in farmland a seed comes up, grows and opens into a sunflower - with a block of room above for the head; bone meal hurries it. The Oil Press gets the oil out of the seeds, not out of the flower. Chickens and parrots eat them.
jei.nookworks.info.end_seed: Sifted, rarely, from End Gravel: a seed blown in from who knows where. Sown in farmland it comes up as a sprout nobody can name, and what it opens into is decided only then, by chance - most often a flower or a fern, now and then a tall flower, a sweet berry bush, bamboo or corn, once in a long while a wither rose. One seed, one plant. A plant that does not stand in farmland gets dirt under it; a tall one needs a block of room above, or the draw is of the short ones. Bone meal hurries it.
jei.nookworks.info.motor: Set it against a hand-worked machine, such as the Oil Press, and on 20 FE/t its shaft turns the handle twice a second: the Oil Press, the Rice Polisher and the Noodle Maker from a side, the Hand Quern from above or below. Powered, it runs whether or not anything has work, idling at 2 FE/t; a redstone signal stops it. With a Drive Wheel on its shaft, it turns every machine the wheel's belts reach, up to 8, at 20 FE/t for each at work.
jei.nookworks.info.oil_cake: What is left of pressed seeds. A fertilizer: use it on crops like bone meal, or compost it.
jei.nookworks.info.oil_can: Lubricant: vegetable oil with sulfur in it. Use it on a door, trapdoor, fence gate or piston and it opens, shuts and pushes without a sound from then on. Breaking the block takes the oil with it. On a Motor, it silences the Motor's hum.
jei.nookworks.info.iron_pot: A black iron pot for the fire. Put it on a Grill over a lit campfire (it sits down on the grate, in the grill's place), or over fire, magma, lava, a lit furnace, smoker or blast furnace or a running Generator, and pour in water or vegetable oil - bottles, a bucket or a Copper Pipe; one or the other at a time, a bucket at most. An empty bottle or bucket takes it back out. Put the ingredients in one at a time: it starts cooking a moment after the last one. In water: white rice for Bowls of Rice, or potato, carrot, beetroot and Salt for Vegetable Soup - ladle them out with bowls. In oil: two potatoes and Salt for French Fries, raw chicken for Karaage and raw cod for Fried Fish - twice as many with Flour in to coat them - or Breaded Pork for Tonkatsu (take them out with an empty hand), or a Bowl of Rice and an egg for Fried Rice, carrot, potato and Salt for Stir-Fried Vegetables (bowls). A Bowl of Rice keeps its bowl in the pot: the fried rice is served back into it with an empty hand. Each batch uses a little of the water or oil; the rest keeps. Caustic Soda boiled in oil makes Soap; Methanol and Caustic Soda in oil make Biodiesel (glass bottles, or the Methanol's own). Sneak with an empty hand to take the last ingredient back out. There is more besides - udon, stews, potage, doughnuts: the recipe pages show every dish. A hopper above feeds it ingredients, and bowls while a dish waits. Set on a hopper over a fire instead, the pot is heated through the hopper, which takes out each serving in its bowl and the buckets and bottles the cooking freed.

jei.nookworks.info.plate: A white glazed plate for the table. Right-click it with something to eat to serve it; an empty hand takes it off. Udon, tonkatsu, karaage and donuts are set out as the dishes themselves, on a plate or a Wooden Tray.
jei.nookworks.info.tableware: Tableware for the table. Up to four go on one block: click another onto it. For now they stand empty.
jei.nookworks.info.flue: A whole block of a chimney's masonry with the flue down its middle, open only at the top and the bottom. Use it where a chimney goes through a roof or a floor, so there is no gap round it: smoke goes up through it as up the chimney, a chimney stacked on it carries on, and with nothing on it the smoke comes out of its top.
jei.nookworks.info.rice_polisher: Load it with brown rice and right-click it with an empty hand to turn the handle; every three turns a grain comes out as White Rice, and every fourth grain leaves a Rice Bran. They go into a hopper or chest under it, or else one in front of it; with neither they drop out of the chute at its front onto the ground just in front. With a block in the way they gather inside - sneak with an empty hand to take them out - and when that is full the handle stops. A Motor set beside it turns the handle for you.
jei.nookworks.info.hand_quern: Two millstones in a frame, the upper one turned by the bar on its spindle: load it with wheat (a click puts in all you hold) and right-click it with an empty hand to turn it. Every three turns a wheat comes out as Flour; bread crumbles to breadcrumbs. What it grinds goes into a hopper or chest under it, or one in front of it; with neither it drops out of the spout at its front onto the ground just in front, and with a block in the way it gathers inside (sneak with an empty hand to take it out). A Motor above or below it turns it by its spindle. Flour for bread and noodles, before there is a powered Crusher.
jei.nookworks.info.noodle_maker: A hand-cranked noodle machine: put in Udon Dough and turn the handle with an empty hand. Its rollers press the dough thin and its cutters cut it into Raw Udon, two for each dough, every four turns. Boil the noodles in the Iron Pot with dried kelp for the broth. Output and Motors work as on the Rice Polisher.
jei.nookworks.info.bread_dough: Flour, a water bucket, Salt and sugar knead into three balls of dough. Set them on a Wooden Tray - four to a tray - and leave them: in three minutes they rise, swelling as they go. Take them off with an empty hand and bake the Risen Dough in a furnace or smoker for bread.
jei.nookworks.info.wooden_tray: A board with a low rim, for the kitchen table or counter. It takes up to four things to eat, one to a place: Bread Dough to rise (in three minutes), loaves, a bowl of rice, a cutlet - whatever is to be served. Right-click with the food to put it on; an empty hand takes off the last one, and sneaking, everything. It goes with the table under it. A hopper above can put things on it; standing on a hopper, it is emptied of anything but dough still rising.

It lies on its side, the way it is set against a block or the way you face; bales stack into a storehouse pile. Straw breaks a fall like hay, and burns.
jei.nookworks.info.corn_kernels: Corn's seed: kernels dried on the ear. Found now and then when soil is sifted, or shelled from an ear on a crafting table, four to an ear. Plant them in farmland: corn grows a second block tall, tassels, and bears two to four ears when ripe. Broken before then it gives nothing back - the kernel has gone into the plant. Chickens and parrots eat them, and the Oil Press gets a little oil out of them.
jei.nookworks.info.ventilation_fan: Set it into a wall, its guard to the room, and click it (or give it a redstone signal) to run it. It draws the smoke and steam of pots, grills, generators and electric furnaces up to six blocks in front of it, and sends it out of its back - into the open, or into the Ducts behind it. It is for the look of a kitchen or a workshop - though a Barter Terminal's room needs one in its wall.
jei.nookworks.info.ventilation_fan.witho: Set it into a wall, its guard to the room, and click it (or give it a redstone signal) to run it. It draws the smoke and steam of pots, grills, generators and electric furnaces up to six blocks in front of it, and sends it out of its back - into the open, or into the Ducts behind it. It is for the look of a kitchen or a workshop: nothing needs it.
jei.nookworks.info.range_hood: Hang it over the stove, up to three blocks above the pot or grill. The smoke and steam rise into it instead of the room, and go up the Duct or Chimney on top of it. It is for the look of a kitchen: nothing needs it.
jei.nookworks.info.duct: Galvanized sheet-steel ducting. It joins other ducts, the back of a Ventilation Fan, the top of a Range Hood and the side of a Chimney, and carries their smoke: it comes out where a run of duct ends in the open, or out of the chimney. It joins a Barter Terminal on any face too, and carries its Nether air to the fan in its room.
jei.nookworks.info.duct.without_barter_t: Galvanized sheet-steel ducting. It joins other ducts, the back of a Ventilation Fan, the top of a Range Hood and the side of a Chimney, and carries their smoke: it comes out where a run of duct ends in the open, or out of the chimney.
jei.nookworks.info.chimney: A stack of brick or stone with a clay pot on top. Smoke brought to it by a Range Hood or Ducts comes out of the pot; built over a lit campfire, furnace, smoker, blast furnace or a running Generator, it smokes of itself. Where it goes through a roof, use a Flue of the same masonry.
jei.nookworks.info.corn: An ear of corn, picked ripe. Eat it raw, grill it on a campfire or the Grill, or make it into Corn Potage; pigs like it too. Corn is not planted from the ear but from its kernels: shell an ear on a crafting table for four.
jei.nookworks.info.onion: Found now and then when soil is sifted. Plant the onion itself in farmland, as a potato. It goes into Cream Stew and Corn Potage, and in place of beetroot into Vegetable Soup, which then makes three bowls, not two.
jei.nookworks.info.rice_bran: Rubbed off brown rice in the Rice Polisher. Press it for vegetable oil, use it on crops like bone meal, compost it, or feed it to chickens.
jei.nookworks.info.nukadoko: A tub of salted rice bran for pickling. Bury carrots or beetroots in it (four at most) and leave them for about ten minutes: they come out as nukazuke, a pickle that fills you up for longer. Take the pickled ones out with an empty hand; sneak to take everything out. A hopper above can bury vegetables, and one underneath takes out the pickles.
jei.nookworks.info.soap: Vegetable oil boiled with caustic soda: put a bottle of oil and a Caustic Soda in a hot Iron Pot. Scrub a dyed block with it - wool, carpet, a bed, stained glass or panes, terracotta - and the dye washes out. On anything else it washes off the oil from an Oil Can and a Fireproof Coating.
jei.nookworks.info.soap.without_kitchen: Vegetable oil and caustic soda: a bottle of oil and a Caustic Soda, crafted together, make two. Scrub a dyed block with it - wool, carpet, a bed, stained glass or panes, terracotta - and the dye washes out. On anything else it washes off the oil from an Oil Can and a Fireproof Coating.
Raw meat and fish can make you ill a minute or two after eating them: chicken always, pork half the time, beef, mutton and rabbit now and then (milder), fish rarely (a parasite).
nookworks.configuration.campfiresPlacedU: A campfire or soul campfire a player sets down starts out unlit: light it with flint and steel, a fire charge or a burning arrow. Off, it is lit as soon as it is placed, as in vanilla.
nookworks.configuration.recipeChoice.too: When a crafting grid matches recipes that make different things (two mods' recipes for the same ingredients), a button by the result lets you pick which to make, and your pick is remembered. Off by itself when Polymorph is installed, which does the same.
nookworks.configuration.chestSortAllowed: Players may sort a chest, barrel or shulker box with the Sort button on its screen (each player can also hide the button in their own settings). Off, no one sees the button and the server sorts nothing.
nookworks.configuration.traderVillageMap: How likely a Wandering Trader is to sell a map to the nearest village to a player who has never been in one: 0 never, 1 every trader.
nookworks.configuration.endSeedModFlower: An End Seed may also open into other mods' flowers, with the same share of the draw as vanilla's flowers. Off, only what the nookworks:end_seed data map lists.
nookworks.configuration.endSeedLeftOutMo: Mods Left Out of End Seeds
Mod ids whose flowers an End Seed never opens into, for a mod's flower that should not grow wild.
nookworks.configuration.flourBakery.tool: Bread, cookies, cake and pumpkin pie are made of flour: bread from dough that rises and is baked. Off, the vanilla recipes from wheat come back. Read at startup.
nookworks.configuration.edibleRawFoods.t: Kelp, sugar cane, sugar, salt, short grass, mushrooms and fungi (the red mushroom is poisonous), honeycomb and cocoa beans can be eaten as they are. Read at startup.
nookworks.configuration.worldMenu.toolti: A Nookworks Parts button on the Create World screen (its More tab) lets each new world leave parts of the mod out, kept in the world's folder (serverconfig/nookworks-features.json). A part switched off under Parts of the Mod is off in every world. Off, there is no button and every world has the parts set there alone. Read at startup.
nookworks.configuration.features.tooltip: Parts a modpack can switch off, in every world (restart to apply); a world can leave out more when it is made. Off, a part's items are made by no recipe, sit in no creative tab, are hidden in JEI and come out of no sifting or trade, and its advancements are gone; what a world already holds stays and works.
nookworks.configuration.features.kitchen: The kitchen and its fields: rice, corn and onions, the pot, grill, tray and nukadoko, the Rice Polisher, Hand Quern and Noodle Maker, the dishes, the range hood and chimney. The flour bakery goes with it; Soap, with no pot, is then mixed in the crafting grid. The Oil Press, Ventilation Fan and Ducts stay.
nookworks.configuration.features.storage: The Storage Barrels and their upgrades.
nookworks.configuration.features.sorting: The Item Sorter, the Precision Sorter and the sorter gears.
nookworks.configuration.features.warps.t: The Item Warps and the Horizontal Item Warps.
nookworks.configuration.features.magnets: The Magnet, the Advanced Magnet and the Magnet Chest. The Absorption Pad cannot be made either, as its recipe takes a Magnet.
nookworks.configuration.features.hammers: The hammers, Velarium's too; with them goes picking up a spawner with Silk Touch. The Earthmover enchantment stays, and does nothing without a hammer.
nookworks.configuration.features.spawner: The Spawner Link Sender and Receiver and the Spawner Controller.
nookworks.configuration.features.mob_bot: The Mob Bottle and the Spawn Egg Brewer. The Barter Terminal cannot be made either, as its piglins go into their room by a Mob Bottle.
nookworks.configuration.features.liquid_: Experience Pipes and Tanks, the Absorption Pad, the Repair Box, and Liquid Experience in buckets and bottles. Machines still keep the experience they make.
nookworks.configuration.features.printin: The Printing Press, posters and labels.
nookworks.configuration.features.dark_ma: Dark Matter and the Warp Anchor.
nookworks.configuration.features.daemon_: The Dock-a-Daemon Door and its Destination Panel.

jei.nookworks.info.wood_vinegar: Dry-distil wood: put a log in the Sealed Retort with a glass bottle in a reagent slot, and it leaves charcoal and a bottle of wood vinegar. The Vacuum Distiller takes the methanol out of it. Used on a field (the farmland, or a crop on it), a bottle is sprinkled over the 5x5 square about it: for three days rabbits will not raid the carrots there, and nourished soil gives up its richness half as fast.
jei.nookworks.info.methanol: Wood alcohol, distilled from wood vinegar in the Vacuum Distiller. With a Caustic Soda it turns vegetable oil into biodiesel: in a powered Stirring Tank with oil piped in (the biodiesel comes out of its top into a Copper Pipe), or by hand in the Iron Pot.
jei.nookworks.info.methanol.without_kitc: Wood alcohol, distilled from wood vinegar in the Vacuum Distiller. With a Caustic Soda it turns vegetable oil into biodiesel in a powered Stirring Tank with oil piped in (the biodiesel comes out of its top into a Copper Pipe).
jei.nookworks.info.biodiesel_bottle: The fuel a Diesel Generator runs on, which gets twice a Generator's power out of it. Elsewhere it burns as long as vegetable oil - by the bucket in a furnace or a Generator, bottled in a Generator only, or piped into a Generator's tank. Made in a Stirring Tank (methanol and caustic soda in its slots, oil piped in) or by hand in the Iron Pot. One Caustic Soda serves four batches, a bucket of oil: it is the catalyst, barely used up.
jei.nookworks.info.biodiesel_bottle.with: The fuel a Diesel Generator runs on, which gets twice a Generator's power out of it. jei.nookworks.info.nook_dowsing_rod: A dowsing rod tuned to cinnabar, which is found only in the sulfur caves, deep underground. Use it and it searches out to 6,400 blocks for the nearest of them; then its needle points there as a lodestone compass points, and it says how far off they are and how deep. Use it again to search from where you stand. In the caves already, it trembles. Each find wears it a little; mend it with copper ingots.
jei.nookworks.info.wool_shears: Spring shears with brass handles, made for wool. Vanilla's shears cut a sheep's lead before its wool; these shear a sheep on a lead and leave the lead as it is, held or tied. Each shearing has a one-in-three chance of a wool more, and Fortune adds another chance a level (about one more wool at Fortune III). In a dispenser they shear the sheep in front of it, its lead left on. Use them on a vine and it stops spreading; vanilla's shears leave it growing. On the tip of a cave vine, a weeping or twisting vine or kelp they trim it, as vanilla's shears do, and it grows no further. They cut nothing else. Mended with brass at an anvil; they take Unbreaking and Mending too.

jei.nookworks.info.camera: A brass camera. Hold right-click to raise it to your eye: the screen becomes its viewfinder, the world in a 4:3 frame with the HUD put away. Left-click takes what is in the frame. The camera keeps its last 9 photos; a tenth pushes the oldest out, and a photo never printed is gone for good when it goes. Open a Printing Press with the camera in your inventory and its Photos page lists them: pick a photo and a size from 1×1 to 4×3 blocks (the middle of the photo, cut to that shape), then print it as a poster, with a sheet of Fine Paper and the four inks. Print as many copies as you like. In third-person view it takes the view you see, yourself in it.

nookworks.configuration.playerPhotos.too: Cameras take photos, which players' games send the server, and the server shows them to others on posters. Off, cameras take none and the server sends no photo to anyone: posters of them show blank paper. An operator can take one photo out with /nookworks photo remove <number> (its number is in a poster's tooltip with F3+H).
